newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour has 12 bln stg black hole - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour has 12 bln stg black hole - Clarke.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Friday challenged Labour to explain a 12.0 billion stg "black hole" in their spending plans, based on plans to allow higher local authorities spending on housing.
The Labour Party has pledged to allow local government more funds for council house building through the release of capital receipts.
"This is a firm commitment which would total 2.5 billion pounds each year over the next parliament," Clarke said in a statement.
"Tony Blair has now admitted that it would count as spending and that it would increase borrowing or taxes," he said.
Clarke repeated the Conservative allegations that Labour's manifesto would leave unexplained how they would make good a 12.0 billion pound shortfall from their spending plans.
Earlier this week, Labour claimed the Conservative spending plans would cost 15.5 billion stg.
The UK faces a general election on May 1. The ruling Conservatives are lagging their Labour rivals by more than 20 points in the opinion polls.
